result:
I'll stage the project from outcomes. Here is the list for you to rank. I won't write any roadmap text until you answer.

## Outcomes (unranked)

These are candidates drawn from the spec's §3 Rulings, stated as what you get.

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A Parquet filing-index catalog for a chosen range of archived quarters, kept with the original index files | R1, R3 | Request count is small: about one listing plus one file per quarter, so a 1993–2026 range is roughly 270 requests, or about 1.5 minutes at 3 req/s. I can't state data volume without the file sizes, which the probe below would measure. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added to the catalog as the SEC lists them, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 250 files a year. Catching up after an outage costs seconds of request budget. |
| O3 | Reprocessing stored index files after a parser change, with no new SEC downloads | R6 | Compute only. Stage 1's real run measures it. |
| O4 | Weekly reconciliation that applies SEC corrections to closed quarters, with any removed filings held until you approve them | R7, R10 | Re-reads every quarter weekly (same request count as O1). It also costs your time for each withdrawal approval. |
| O5 | Readers see complete per-quarter versions through one active pointer, never half-written files | R9 | Small. Most of the cost is testing. |
| O6 | All SEC traffic from every pipeline shares one request budget at 3 req/s with your User-Agent | R8 | No extra SEC cost by design. |
| O7 | Unattended operation on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, alerts, runbooks, rollback | R4, §7 | Azure spend can't be estimated until something is deployed. The stage that deploys it measures the cost. |

**R5 and R11 are not outcomes.** R5 (shared code across modes) and R11 (defaults that change only through configuration review) are constraints on how the system is built. I'll record them as constraints that hold across every stage.

## Tracks

**Track A, known progression: one track for everything.** I'm not splitting off a separate track because every outcome depends on the O1 catalog. O7 has no use on its own, so these are dependencies rather than unrelated questions. Stage 1 would be the core: O1 on one real quarter plus one real daily file, run locally, with the measured cost recorded. The later stages build out from there. Alerts, runbooks, deployment and fault-injection suites go into named later stages, not into stage 1.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 in a uv workspace (repo).
- Platform: Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor), per the ADR. Note that the ADR and the spec are both still marked **Proposed**, and spec §7 step 1 says to accept them first. Should I treat Azure as decided?
- Roadmap file: `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The name comes from the spec's filename stem.

**Package layout doesn't match the spec.** The repo has four packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`, `-ingest`). Spec §4.9 puts everything in `sec-edgar-ingest`. I'll record whichever layout you choose as a choice made.

## Optional probe

To pin down O1's data volume, I'd like to fetch one `full-index` `index.json` listing and send a HEAD request for one quarter's `master.idx`. The SEC requires a User-Agent with contact details, so I'd need you to tell me what identity to put in it. I'll only run this if you say yes.

## Your call

Please do these in one reply:
1. Rank O1–O7.
2. Confirm the single known-progression track, or change it.
3. Answer the Azure-acceptance and package-layout points.
4. Say yes or no to the probe.
